research_question: What is the effect of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) interventions, delivered alone or combined with exercise, compared with control, on fear of falling in community-dwelling older people, measured immediately after the intervention?
treatment_label: CBT intervention (alone or combined with exercise)
control_label: Control (usual care, waitlist, or attention/education control)
outcome_description: Fear of falling or falls-related self-efficacy measured immediately post-intervention
positive_direction: Reduced fear of falling / greater falls-related self-efficacy favoring the CBT intervention
search_queries: cognitive behavioral therapy fear of falling older adults randomized trial
matter of balance falls efficacy community elderly controlled trial
CBT exercise fear of falling intervention trial outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials evaluating cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) or multicomponent behavioural programmes (alone or combined with exercise) in community-dwelling older adults aged 60 and older
Studies comparing the intervention against a control group (usual care, waitlist, no intervention, or an attention/discussion/education control)
Studies reporting quantitative post-intervention outcome data on fear of falling or falls-related self-efficacy/confidence
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, opinion pieces, or theoretical papers)
No comparison between an eligible CBT/behaviour-change intervention and a control condition (e.g., single-arm studies, or exercise/education-only arms with no cognitive-behavioural component)
No quantitative outcome data allowing calculation of an effect size for fear of falling or falls efficacy (e.g., lacking post-intervention means and SDs, sample sizes, or test statistics)
Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g., institutionalized/hospitalized patients, participants under 60 years of age, or non-fall-related interventions)
moderators_to_extract: Intervention type (CBT alone vs CBT combined with exercise/multicomponent)
Control group type (inactive/usual care vs active/attention control)
Outcome measurement instrument (FES-I vs ABC/mFES vs single-item)
effect_size_note: Pool as SMD (Hedges' g) using a random-effects model. SMD < 0 indicates less fear of falling (favours intervention). For fear/concern scales (e.g., FES-I), higher scores mean more fear; for confidence/efficacy scales (e.g., ABC, mFES, FES-S), reverse score direction so lower values always indicate less fear. Instrument preference order: FES-I (or Short FES-I) > mFES / FES / FES-S / ABC > single-item question. Extract post-intervention means and SDs at the first assessment immediately after intervention completion. Divide shared control N equally for multi-arm CBT comparisons. Adjust for clustering in cluster-randomized trials if not already accounted for.
